lead: your next fifteen years are allocated. a sister's move, two careers, an old woman's last address — worked out in conversations you were not in, and exactly one line of it was ever put to you out loud.
sun: the arrangement you are actually a party to was entered properly: a table, a person opposite, one sentence, and no occasion since on which it came up. twenty-two years of that holding in plain view is all the evidence anybody needed. people do not plan against somebody who might go. they plan against a fixed point, and you demonstrated the fixing yourself, in public, once, and it reads across everything you never mentioned.
moon: nothing was stated about your later years, and an unstated future reads as room. The Empty District hands over nothing and refuses nothing; whoever arrives first fills it, and what is filled gets called long settled. by the time the move came up, your part in it reached you as a reminder — the tone of somebody confirming a thing arranged years ago, which in her account it was.
pull: you are a party to one thing and a fixed point in ten others. the ten have no second side: nobody to ask, nothing to be let out of, no evening on which they began.
tension: the one you entered has no exit in it, as you knew going in. the ten have no exit either, for the reverse reason — nothing was undertaken, which leaves nobody with standing to release you and nothing on record to release. correcting your sister means telling her that six years of her planning ran on an inference, that the inference was sound, and that you would have agreed had anybody asked. the sentence gets no further than that.
cost: a decade of somebody else's planning rests on you and comes out right, which is rare enough to explain the ten. they run on an inference rather than on anything you said, and the inference has been sound every time it was made. so you discharge them at the weight of the real one, and the real one is the only place a release could ever come from.

lead: at the eightieth, four of them are round the same table, and no two accounts of that year agree. you took all four separately, years apart, each with your word attached.
sun: discretion is a habit, and habits soften. each of them got a sentence back at the time, out loud, in the room: this goes nowhere, from me, ever. put that way it converts on the spot from kindness into terms, and terms here do not weaken as the reason for them recedes. so you are running four agreements, entered years apart, one person each, and the parties do not know the others are parties.
moon: more came in than any of them handed over. the wording, the half-beat before the wording, what the room was doing underneath it — The Listener takes the whole sound rather than the sentence, so a fair amount of what you carry was heard rather than told. your word covers the told part exactly. nothing in you sorts the remainder into a different pile.
pull: four people believe you are agreeing with them. what you have is four accounts of one year, all sincere, all incompatible, and a promise sitting on each.
tension: in the spring the four of them will settle, for good, who was responsible for that year, and they will get it wrong in two places, and you will be sitting there. correcting it means saying which of them told you what, and when, and what state they were in. no one is lying; each works from what they were handed. nothing in that room is an exposure. it is four agreements and a question of which to break.
cost: people hand you the true version early, at the first opportunity, and they do it because they can hear the undertaking arriving before you have finished replying. the material accumulates. the man the spring lands on will carry it for the rest of his life, and the correction was in the room the whole time, in somebody who cannot produce it.

lead: first sunday, twenty-six years, the same upstairs room. nine come now and forty used to, and the ones who stopped coming in their forties can tell you which month they left.
sun: nobody drifted into the date. the two of you fixed it in the first year, out loud, as a term of the thing — first sunday, whatever else is happening — and a term does not adjust itself for attendance. so it goes ahead at nine as it went ahead at forty, in weather, through both of your bad decades, and the wording has not been looked at since.
moon: past a certain number of years an interval stops being an event and turns into a unit. children get placed against it, illnesses get dated by it, people who left in their thirties count backwards from it. The Drum asks nobody to keep time by it. the beat goes out, and the keeping happens somewhere past the room, unannounced, among people who have not been upstairs in twenty years.
pull: the room holds nine. the interval holds forty. you agreed the date with one man in the first year, and he has been out of it for eleven.
tension: the content emptied out somewhere around year fifteen, and every person in that room knows it. the difficulty is elsewhere. ending it takes a unit out of other people's counting — the woman who dates her recovery from a first sunday, the pair who worked out when their father went by counting back — and word of it would reach them secondhand. no wording exists for finishing a thing that has stopped being an event and become a measurement.
cost: nothing has had to be organised to keep it going — no reminder, no committee, nobody whose job it was — and a thing that regular gets used as infrastructure by people who never joined. the hour is booked out of every month left to you. what stopped being true fifteen years ago has no bearing on the first sunday, and the first sunday is what people have.

lead: the place has been open for eleven years and he has never taken it. you put it to him once, at a table, in about a dozen words, and nothing since has been able to close what you said.
sun: there is a place here for you, for as long as you want it — said level, to a man in the position you had been in, nothing pushing either of you. no other register exists in you for saying anything, and an offer made in it is not a gesture. it took effect in the room. eleven years on the terms are unreduced, because nothing you enter comes back round to be trimmed.
moon: an opening has to be kept clear to be real. so the bench sits, and the work that belongs on it goes to people on short terms who do it adequately and go. what you offered was room, and room means a section of the operation answering to nobody, earning nothing, and unfillable without cancelling what it was offered as. The Void does not do a partial version.
pull: the place is genuinely his and genuinely open, and it has cost you a bench for eleven years, and he cannot break an offer, only decline to arrive at it.
tension: asking what he intends would date it, and a date is the one component your offer does not have. the day it acquires one it stops being the thing he was given and turns into a demand with a clock on it. so every couple of years he checks, lightly, that the place is where he left it, and you confirm that it is, and the arithmetic of eleven years has no place in a conversation that light.
cost: somebody can come back at eleven years and find an offer exactly as it was put to him — same wording, nothing quietly reduced in the interval — which almost nothing survives. two people who would have taken the bench were sent elsewhere. the place is reserved by a man who is not coming, and it goes on being real, which is the only way you hold anything open.
